correctness.rationale: Every nonscalar 2x2 matrix is cyclic, and its matrix centralizer is span{I,A}; each commuting nonscalar family member therefore has a unique u_j I+v_j A, v_j!=0. Any nonscalar conjugate has entries (a,b;c,t-a), with bc=a(t-a)-d; all offdiagonals nonzero iff a not in Z and all diagonal shifts nonzero iff a not in E. For each eligible a, precisely q-1 nonzero (b,c) products occur, giving N=(q-1)(q-|E union Z|). Centralizer-orbit division establishes the change-of-basis count. The q=2^m obstruction partitions field into pairs {s,s+1}; q=5 pair has E={0,1,2,4}, Z={3}. Independent exhaustive matrix quadruple enumeration over F5 found zero admissible common conjugates and exactly eight per individual member.
